atoms.text: This guide configures the Duplicata replication service to copy new objects from the bucket prod-orders-east to the bucket prod-orders-west for disaster recovery. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Duplicata assumes, and no bucket policy is changed on either bucket. Create a role named duplicata-replication-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal duplicata.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObjectVersion and storage:ListBucket on prod-orders-east, and storage:PutObject on prod-orders-west/*. Leave the existing bucket policies on both buckets as they are, because the role's permissions are sufficient within a single account. In the replication rule, set the role's identifier as the execution identity and filter on the key prefix orders/. Enable versioning on both buckets before saving the rule, because replication works on object version identifiers. After saving, upload a test object under orders/ and confirm that a replica with the same key and checksum appears in prod-orders-west within a few minutes. The source object's replication status metadata should then read COMPLETED.

This guide configures the Duplicata replication service to copy new objects from the bucket prod-orders-east to the bucket prod-orders-west for disaster recovery. Access is granted only through each bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal duplicata.svc.example, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy on prod-orders-east that allows that principal to perform storage:GetObjectVersion and storage:ListBucket on the bucket and its objects. Add a statement to the policy on prod-orders-west that allows the same principal to perform storage:PutObject on prod-orders-west/*. Do not create or attach any role, because the bucket policies are sufficient within a single account. In the replication rule, set the service principal as the execution identity and filter on the key prefix orders/. Enable versioning on both buckets before saving the rule, because replication works on object version identifiers. After saving, upload a test object under orders/ and confirm that a replica with the same key and checksum appears in prod-orders-west within a few minutes. The source object's replication status metadata should then read COMPLETED.

This guide sets up the Nightvault backup service to write nightly database export files to the bucket db-backups-archive. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Nightvault assumes, and the bucket policy on db-backups-archive stays unchanged. Create a role named nightvault-writer-role with a trust policy that lets the service principal nightvault.svc.example assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject and storage:DeleteObject on db-backups-archive/exports/*, and storage:ListBucket on the bucket itself. The delete permission is needed because the service removes exports older than 35 days after each successful run. Register the role's identifier in the Nightvault job definition as the identity used for all bucket calls. Set the job schedule to 02:00 UTC and the destination to the prefix exports/. Run the job once manually and check that a file named with the export date appears under exports/ with a non-zero size. On the following night, confirm that the retention step lists the prefix and deletes only objects past the 35-day limit.

Add storage:ListBucket on the bucket itself to the same statement or a second one. The delete permission is needed because the service removes exports older than 35 days after each successful run. Register the service principal in the Nightvault job definition as the identity used for all bucket calls. Set the job schedule to 02:00 UTC and the destination to the prefix exports/. On the following night, confirm that the retention step lists the prefix and deletes only objects past the 35-day limit.

This guide lets the Rehydra restore service read backup data from the bucket dr-standby-backups so it can rebuild a standby database cluster. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Rehydra assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named rehydra-restore-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal rehydra.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on dr-standby-backups/snapshots/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket. Do not grant any write or delete action, since the restore workflow never modifies the backup set. Enter the role's identifier in the restore plan as the identity for reading snapshots. Set the restore plan to use the newest snapshot under snapshots/ unless a specific snapshot key is given. Start a test restore into an empty standby cluster and monitor the service log for the list and read requests it issues. A successful run ends with the log entry restore-complete and a matching checksum for every object read.

This guide configures the Logkeep archival service to copy application log files into the bucket logs-retention with a write-once retention period. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Logkeep assumes, and the bucket policy on logs-retention is not modified. Create a role named logkeep-archive-role whose trust policy allows the service principal logkeep.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject and storage:PutObjectRetention on logs-retention/archive/*. Grant no delete permission, so archived objects can only expire through their retention setting. Object lock must already be enabled on the bucket, because it cannot be added to an existing bucket afterwards. Configure Logkeep to use the role's identifier and to apply a 365-day compliance retention to every object it writes. Point the service at the source prefix app-logs/ and the destination prefix archive/. After the first hourly run, attempt to delete one archived object and confirm the request is denied until retention expires.

This guide configures the Logkeep archival service to copy application log files into the bucket logs-retention with a write-once retention period. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal logkeep.svc.example, and no IAM role is created. Edit the policy on logs-retention and add a statement that allows that principal to perform storage:PutObject and storage:PutObjectRetention on logs-retention/archive/*. Grant no delete permission, so archived objects can only expire through their retention setting. Object lock must already be enabled on the bucket, because it cannot be added to an existing bucket afterwards. Configure Logkeep to use the service principal as its identity and to apply a 365-day compliance retention to every object it writes. Point the service at the source prefix app-logs/ and the destination prefix archive/. After the first hourly run, attempt to delete one archived object and confirm the request is denied until retention expires. No role, trust policy, or identity-based policy is part of this setup.

This guide sets up the Mirrorline service to replicate media assets, including tags and delete markers, from the bucket media-primary to the bucket media-replica. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Mirrorline assumes, and neither bucket policy is changed. Create a role named mirrorline-sync-role with a trust policy that lets the service principal mirrorline.svc.example assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:GetObjectVersion, storage:GetObjectVersionTagging, and storage:ListBucket on media-primary. In the same policy, allow storage:PutObject, storage:PutObjectTagging, and storage:ReplicateDelete on media-replica/*. Turn on versioning for both buckets, since delete markers are only produced on versioned buckets. Set the replication rule to cover the whole bucket and enable the delete marker option. Provide the role's identifier as the rule's execution identity. Test by uploading a tagged image, deleting it, and confirming that media-replica shows the same tag and then the same delete marker.

This guide sets up the Mirrorline service to replicate media assets, including tags and delete markers, from the bucket media-primary to the bucket media-replica. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies on the two buckets, which name the service principal mirrorline.svc.example, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy on media-primary that allows that principal to perform storage:GetObjectVersion, storage:GetObjectVersionTagging, and storage:ListBucket. Add a statement to the policy on media-replica that allows the same principal to perform storage:PutObject, storage:PutObjectTagging, and storage:ReplicateDelete on media-replica/*. Turn on versioning for both buckets, since delete markers are only produced on versioned buckets. Set the replication rule to cover the whole bucket and enable the delete marker option. Provide the service principal as the rule's execution identity. Test by uploading a tagged image, deleting it, and confirming that media-replica shows the same tag and then the same delete marker.

This guide lets the Sharesnap backup service store incremental backups of a network file share in the bucket fileshare-backups. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Sharesnap assumes, and the bucket policy remains as it is. Create a role named sharesnap-backup-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal sharesnap.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload, and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on fileshare-backups/chunks/*. Add storage:ListBucket and storage:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket itself. Sharesnap splits changed files into 64 MiB parts, so multipart permissions are required for any file above that size. Enter the role's identifier in the backup policy and set the destination prefix to chunks/. Add a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads after 3 days. Run a full backup, modify one file, run an incremental backup, and confirm that only the changed parts are uploaded.

This guide configures the Bulkcopy service to run a one-time backfill that copies existing objects from the bucket legacy-records to the bucket records-dr. The job reads a manifest file from the bucket copy-inventory and writes a completion report back to it. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Bulkcopy assumes, and no bucket policy on any of the three buckets is changed. Create a role named bulkcopy-job-role whose trust policy allows the service principal bulkcopy.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:GetObject on legacy-records/* and copy-inventory/manifests/*. In the same policy, allow storage:PutObject on records-dr/* and copy-inventory/reports/*. Create the job with the role's identifier as its execution identity and the manifest key manifests/backfill-001.csv. Set the job to preserve the original last-modified timestamp in object metadata. When the job finishes, open the report under reports/ and verify that the failed-object count is zero.

This guide configures the Bulkcopy service to run a one-time backfill that copies existing objects from the bucket legacy-records to the bucket records-dr. The job reads a manifest file from the bucket copy-inventory and writes a completion report back to it. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies on the three buckets, which name the service principal bulkcopy.svc.example, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policies on legacy-records and copy-inventory that allows that principal to perform storage:GetObject on legacy-records/* and copy-inventory/manifests/*. Add statements allowing the same principal to perform storage:PutObject on records-dr/* and copy-inventory/reports/*. Create the job with the service principal as its execution identity and the manifest key manifests/backfill-001.csv. Set the job to preserve the original last-modified timestamp in object metadata. When the job finishes, open the report under reports/ and verify that the failed-object count is zero. Each bucket policy should be checked to confirm that it lists only the actions named above.

This guide configures the Cfgsafe service to back up per-tenant configuration files into the bucket tenant-config-backups, with each tenant limited to its own prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Cfgsafe assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named cfgsafe-tenant-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal cfgsafe.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject and storage:GetObject on tenant-config-backups/tenant-a/*. Add a condition to the allow statement requiring that every write request carry the server-side encryption header with the value AES256. Add storage:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted by a prefix condition to tenant-a/. Register the role's identifier in the Cfgsafe tenant settings and set the destination prefix to tenant-a/. Trigger a backup and confirm that the stored object reports AES256 as its encryption type. Then send a test write without the header and confirm that it is rejected.
